root_cause.text: In the ipset hash set deletion path (`mtype_del()` in `net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_hash_gen.h`), the code only freed a bucket when `n->pos == 0 && k == 0`, so buckets whose entries were all deleted but whose `n->pos` still pointed past those removed slots were incorrectly retained as non-empty.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the empty-bucket check from `if (n->pos == 0 && k == 0)` to `if (k == n->pos)`, and the commit message explicitly says `mtype_del()` “counts empty slots below n->pos in k, but it only drops the bucket when both n->pos and k are zero,” missing “buckets whose live entries have all been removed while n->pos still points past deleted slots.”

intent_record.what: In `mtype_del()`, the conditional guarding the bucket removal was changed from `if (n->pos == 0 && k == 0)` to `if (k == n->pos)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the deletion logic so the bucket is freed when the computed count `k` matches the node position `n->pos`, rather than only when both are zero. As a result, removal can now occur for the intended matching element/state instead of being restricted to the first position only.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the direct cause of the bug: it only frees the bucket when the node position is zero and the computed index is zero, so buckets with all deleted entries but a nonzero n->pos are incorrectly retained.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only deletes the bucket when both the node position and computed index are zero. That logic misses buckets whose entries were removed but whose n->pos remained nonzero, leaving empty buckets incorrectly retained.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable deletion logic is present and not corrected. In `mtype_del()`, after finding the matching element, the code does `clear_bit(i, n->used);` and only decrements `n->pos` when the deleted element is the last slot: `if (i + 1 == n->pos) n->pos--;`. It then decides whether the bucket can be freed using `if (n->pos == 0 && k == 0) { ... kfree_rcu(n, rcu); }`, which matches the root cause: a bucket is only freed when `n->pos` is zero, so buckets with all entries deleted but with `n->pos` still pointing past removed slots are retained. There is no alternative check that detects an empty bucket based on the bitmap (`used`) or that compacts/resets `n->pos` after deletions, so the fix is not present in this snippet.
